title: Three UK moth samples did not show a common decrease in catch synchrony after weather adjustment in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether monthly weather adjustment reduced agreement between moth catches at separate UK sites. Three eligible ECN samples covered England in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015 and Scotland in 1992-2003. Models controlled season, site trends and sampling effort. Adding country temperature and rainfall changed mean pair correlations from 0.489 to 0.391, from 0.389 to 0.238 and from 0.652 to 0.718, respectively. Only the later English decrease had a three-test block bootstrap interval above zero: 0.023 to 0.277. The other two change intervals included zero. A stricter sampling rule kept all three directions. Whole-year weather shifts gave smaller decreases in both English tests, but the rank score was only 0.083. Late Scotland failed the overlap rule. The results do not establish a common regional decrease. Shared capture effects, species composition, coarse weather, few years and one Scottish pair limit interpretation. We test no causal climate-change effect, air pollutant or daily extreme. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and retrieval instructions. External raw data and the derived monthly database stay outside the publication.
